author: Lafresnaye, 1841

art.subject: Eurasian Bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula griseiventris), adult male in winter: glossy black cap from the forehead to the crown, black around the bill base and on the chin; cheeks, ear-coverts and throat rose-red; nape, mantle and back blue-grey; breast, flanks and belly grey like the back, with no red; rump and undertail coverts white; wings glossy black with a broad pale grey-white bar on the greater coverts; tail glossy black. Bill short, thick, rounded and black; dark eye; legs dark brown. The female has the same black cap but a grey-brown body and no red.
art.pose: perched in a bare tree nibbling buds, side view
art.scene: Korean mountain woodland in winter, bare deciduous branches with swelling buds and a little snow; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Plump, bull-necked finch, a little larger than a sparrow, with a big rounded head and short neck. Bill black, very short, thick and stubby, rounded on the culmen, much shorter than the head. Legs short, dark brown. Wings fairly short; tail medium length, black, square to slightly notched. Moves slowly, nibbling buds and seeds in trees and shrubs. In flight a square white rump contrasts with the black tail.
avoid: Do not paint red or pink on the breast and belly; this race is grey below, red only on the cheeks and throat.
Do not paint a conical, pointed bill; it is short, thick and rounded.
Do not omit the white rump and the pale wing-bar.
Do not extend the black cap down over the throat; only the chin is black.
